item.title: Fight, pistol whipping, and gunfire erupt in Atmore restaurant district
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Atmore police are investigating an incident that began with a physical altercation and escalated into gunfire in the city's restaurant corridor. According to WKRG News 5, the incident unfolded at the Waffle House parking lot, where someone was reportedly pistol whipped during a fight. The situation then moved to a nearby Popeye's Louisiana Kitchen…
item.content:encoded:
Atmore police are investigating an incident that began with a physical altercation and escalated into gunfire in the city's restaurant corridor.

According to WKRG News 5, the incident unfolded at the Waffle House parking lot, where someone was reportedly pistol whipped during a fight. The situation then moved to a nearby Popeye's Louisiana Kitchen location, where the suspect allegedly discharged a firearm.

Atmore Police Department has not yet released details about injuries, arrests, or the circumstances leading to the confrontation. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Sunny skies, upper 80s expected Sunday in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A pleasant autumn pattern is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, with sunny skies and a high near 88 expected Sunday, according to the National Weather Service. Winds will remain calm, picking up only slightly to around 5 mph from the northwest in the afternoon. Sunday night will stay mostly clear with temperatures dropping to near…
item.content:encoded:
A pleasant autumn pattern is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, with sunny skies and a high near 88 expected Sunday, according to the National Weather Service. Winds will remain calm, picking up only slightly to around 5 mph from the northwest in the afternoon.

Sunday night will stay mostly clear with temperatures dropping to near 60, providing relief from the summer heat. The cooler, drier air mass moving into the region is expected to stick around through the start of the week, bringing below-normal overnight temperatures and low humidity levels that should make outdoor activities comfortable.

item.title: Pensacola Interstate Fair returns October 22 with cheaper weekday tickets, full entertainment lineup
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Interstate Fair is gearing up for its 11-day run starting October 22 through November 1, and organizers have announced a slate of changes aimed at drawing more families through the gates. The fair will feature the usual mix of carnival rides, live entertainment, food vendors, and livestock exhibits that draw thousands to the annual…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Interstate Fair is gearing up for its 11-day run starting October 22 through November 1, and organizers have announced a slate of changes aimed at drawing more families through the gates.

The fair will feature the usual mix of carnival rides, live entertainment, food vendors, and livestock exhibits that draw thousands to the annual event each fall. But this year, officials have lowered admission prices for weekday visits, making it more affordable for those who prefer to avoid weekend crowds.

A full entertainment schedule has also been released, though specific performer names and show times were not detailed in the fair's announcement. Fair officials say the combination of lower weekday prices and expanded programming is designed to make the event accessible to more Escambia County residents and visitors from across Northwest Florida.

More details about ticket pricing, entertainment lineups, and special events are expected to be announced as the fair's opening date approaches.

item.title: Cantonment Pumpkin Patch Opens for 31st Season

item.content:encoded:
Fall has officially arrived in Cantonment with the opening of the Allen Memorial Methodist Men Pumpkin Patch, marking three decades of the community tradition. Volunteers from Northview High School's NJROTC program and the Tribal Beat Band helped unload and arrange the pumpkins Thursday, getting the patch ready for the season ahead.

The annual pumpkin patch has become a familiar fixture in the North Escambia area, drawing families looking to pick out gourds for decorating and carving as the season shifts toward Halloween and the holidays. The involvement of local high school groups underscores the community support that keeps the tradition running year after year.

item.title: West Roberts Road Reopens, But Construction Not Yet Complete
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: West Roberts Road in North Escambia is now open to traffic following a series of temporary closures that stretched from late August through the weekend. As of Saturday afternoon, traffic was flowing normally without detours or portable traffic signals, according to local reporting. The reopening marks progress on the $5.16 million West Roberts…
item.content:encoded:
West Roberts Road in North Escambia is now open to traffic following a series of temporary closures that stretched from late August through the weekend. As of Saturday afternoon, traffic was flowing normally without detours or portable traffic signals, according to local reporting.

The reopening marks progress on the $5.16 million West Roberts Road Roadway and Drainage Improvements Project, though work remains ongoing. Drivers who've endured weeks of alternating road closures can expect continued construction activity in the coming weeks as the project nears completion.

Commuters in the area should stay alert for additional temporary closures or traffic management changes as the work continues.

item.title: Escambia County Animal Shelter Offers Free Adoptions Through Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare is running a special adoption promotion this week as part of the Bissell Pet Foundation's "Empty the Shelters" campaign. Dogs and cats that are at least one year old can be adopted at no cost through Wednesday, September 30. The program is designed to help increase adoptions and reduce shelter…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare is running a special adoption promotion this week as part of the Bissell Pet Foundation's "Empty the Shelters" campaign. Dogs and cats that are at least one year old can be adopted at no cost through Wednesday, September 30.

The program is designed to help increase adoptions and reduce shelter overcrowding by removing financial barriers to pet adoption. Eligible animals have already been spayed or neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped, according to the shelter.

For more information about available animals or to complete an adoption, contact the Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare.

item.title: West Florida Library Celebrates Dolly Parton's Literacy Mission With Free Book Giveaway Today
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Friends of the West Florida Public Library are marking music icon Dolly Parton's dedication to childhood literacy today with a special giveaway during their Fall Big Book Sale. Every child who attends the event will receive a free used book, honoring Parton's lifelong commitment to getting books into young readers' hands. Parton has long been…
item.content:encoded:
The Friends of the West Florida Public Library are marking music icon Dolly Parton's dedication to childhood literacy today with a special giveaway during their Fall Big Book Sale. Every child who attends the event will receive a free used book, honoring Parton's lifelong commitment to getting books into young readers' hands.

Parton has long been a champion of literacy initiatives, famously founding her Imagination Library, which mails free books to children in underserved communities. The giveaway ties the local library's efforts to that broader mission of ensuring access to reading material regardless of family income.

The Fall Big Book Sale runs today at the West Florida Public Library, offering used books and the opportunity for families to build home libraries affordably while supporting the Friends of the library, a volunteer organization that funds library programs and services.

item.title: North Escambia Schools Mark Dolly Day With Pink Shirts, Kindness Celebration
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Byrneville Elementary and Ransom Middle School joined schools across the country Friday in celebrating Dolly Day, an annual tribute to the life and legacy of country music icon Dolly Parton. The observance, held each September 25—a date chosen as a play on Parton's famous "9 to 5" song—focuses on honoring her contributions to music and her…
item.content:encoded:
Byrneville Elementary and Ransom Middle School joined schools across the country Friday in celebrating Dolly Day, an annual tribute to the life and legacy of country music icon Dolly Parton.

The observance, held each September 25—a date chosen as a play on Parton's famous "9 to 5" song—focuses on honoring her contributions to music and her lifelong commitment to kindness and compassion. Teachers and staff at both North Escambia schools showed their support by wearing pink shirts throughout the day.

Dolly Day has become a way for schools nationwide to celebrate not just Parton's musical achievements but also the values of generosity and community service she's championed throughout her career.

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia is in for a beautiful weekend, with sunny conditions and pleasant temperatures throughout Saturday and Sunday.

Saturday will see a high near 84 degrees with calm winds becoming northerly around 5 mph in the afternoon. Overnight, conditions remain mild with partly cloudy skies and a low around 63 degrees.

Sunday looks even nicer, with sunny skies and a high near 86 degrees. Winds will remain light, becoming northwest around 5 mph in the afternoon. If you've got outdoor plans, this is the window to make them happen.

According to North Escambia, at least nine Escambia County Fire Rescue trucks and ladder trucks responded to the blaze at 529 West Nine Mile Road just after 9 a.m. Crews…
item.content:encoded:
The state fire marshal's office is now investigating the cause of a fire that broke out Thursday morning at the Chili's location on West Nine Mile Road in Escambia County.

According to North Escambia, at least nine Escambia County Fire Rescue trucks and ladder trucks responded to the blaze at 529 West Nine Mile Road just after 9 a.m. Crews arriving on scene found smoke pouring from the building.

The investigation into what started the fire is ongoing. No additional details about injuries, evacuations, or damage estimates have been released at this time.

The man credits Bright Bridge Ministries with helping him turn his life around. His account highlights how a single traumatic event can cascade into substance abuse,…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola resident is sharing his story of overcoming addiction after an accident and series of poor decisions led him down a difficult path, according to reporting from WKRG-TV 5.

The man credits Bright Bridge Ministries with helping him turn his life around. His account highlights how a single traumatic event can cascade into substance abuse, but also underscores the role local recovery programs play in helping people regain stability.

Bright Bridge Ministries, which operates recovery and support services in the Pensacola area, has become a resource for residents battling addiction. The organization focuses on faith-based recovery and community reintegration.

The story is part of WKRG's ongoing "Drexel on the Road" series, which profiles individuals and organizations making an impact across the Gulf Coast region.

item.title: Bay Minette Elementary Celebrates Young Cancer Survivors During Awareness Month
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Bay Minette Elementary School in Baldwin County is joining a nationwide push to raise awareness about childhood cancer, with school leaders honoring students who've faced the disease. The celebration is part of a broader effort by Baldwin County Public Schools to "go gold" — the official color of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month — in recognition…
item.content:encoded:
Bay Minette Elementary School in Baldwin County is joining a nationwide push to raise awareness about childhood cancer, with school leaders honoring students who've faced the disease. The celebration is part of a broader effort by Baldwin County Public Schools to "go gold" — the official color of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month — in recognition of young people battling or recovering from cancer.

The event gives the school community a chance to recognize the resilience of students who've dealt with a serious health challenge while continuing their education. Childhood cancer survivors often show remarkable strength, and schools across the region are using September as an opportunity to amplify awareness and support for affected families.

Baldwin County schools have embraced the awareness campaign, with multiple campuses displaying gold in various forms throughout the month. The recognition serves both as encouragement for the honored students and as a reminder to the broader school community about the importance of health awareness and support systems for children facing medical hardships.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Three to Apalachicola Water and Sewer District
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the appointment of three new members to the Apalachicola Water and Sewer District board: Jimmy Gander, Torben Madson III, and Mark Milliken. Gander is owner and vice president of JV Gander Oil Company and a former Franklin County School Board member. He's a Florida National Guard veteran who holds a bachelor's…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the appointment of three new members to the Apalachicola Water and Sewer District board: Jimmy Gander, Torben Madson III, and Mark Milliken.

Gander is owner and vice president of JV Gander Oil Company and a former Franklin County School Board member. He's a Florida National Guard veteran who holds a bachelor's degree from the University of West Florida. Madson III owns and manages The PEO Law Firm and serves on the Franklin County Parks and Recreation Board. He earned his law degree from the University of Miami and undergraduate degree from the University of Florida. Milliken, president of Gulf Unmanned Systems Center, is a retired Navy Rear Admiral with experience as a senior manager at Wyle, Inc. and vice president of maritime solutions for Elbit Systems of America. He graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy with a degree in analytical management.

The appointments come as the Apalachicola area continues to manage water resource challenges in the region.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Two to Applied Behavior Analysis Task Force
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Kale Baker and David Brown to the Applied Behavior Analysis Task Force, according to a release from the Governor's Press Office. Baker, who holds a master's degree in social work from Barry University, currently serves as Vice President at Molina Healthcare. He previously worked as Director…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Kale Baker and David Brown to the Applied Behavior Analysis Task Force, according to a release from the Governor's Press Office.

Baker, who holds a master's degree in social work from Barry University, currently serves as Vice President at Molina Healthcare. He previously worked as Director of Regulatory Affairs at Molina Healthcare and held several positions at Magellan Complete Care and Magellan Financial Group, including Senior Director of Account Management and Director of Care Coordination.

Brown, a graduate of New England College and Florida Gulf Coast University with degrees in criminal justice and social work respectively, is President and Co-Founder of Family Initiative. He has also served as Program Coordinator for the Quality Parenting Initiative and Director of Programs for the Children's Network of Southwest Florida.

item.title: DeSantis Names Education Official to Independent Education Commission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis has appointed Kevin O'Farrell, currently the Executive Vice President of Workforce and Strategic Initiatives at Polk State College, to the Commission for Independent Education, according to an announcement from the Governor's Press Office on Friday. O'Farrell brings extensive experience in Florida's education and workforce…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis has appointed Kevin O'Farrell, currently the Executive Vice President of Workforce and Strategic Initiatives at Polk State College, to the Commission for Independent Education, according to an announcement from the Governor's Press Office on Friday.

O'Farrell brings extensive experience in Florida's education and workforce sectors. Before his current role at Polk State, he served as Senior Chancellor for Higher Education and Workforce Development with the Florida Department of Education. He holds a doctorate in curriculum and instruction from the University of South Florida, along with master's degrees in political science and public administration from the same institution.

The appointment is subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate. The Commission for Independent Education oversees Florida's private schools and education programs that operate outside the traditional public school system.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Leon Medical Centers CEO to Fish and Wildlife Commission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis has announced the reappointment of Albert Maury to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, according to the Governor's Press Office. Maury, who serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Leon Medical Centers, LLC, will continue his role on the state commission pending Florida Senate confirmation. Maury…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis has announced the reappointment of Albert Maury to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, according to the Governor's Press Office. Maury, who serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Leon Medical Centers, LLC, will continue his role on the state commission pending Florida Senate confirmation.

Maury brings business and nonprofit leadership experience to the position. He previously served on the Florida International University Board of Trustees and holds a bachelor's degree in finance and accounting from FIU. The reappointment was announced Friday.

The Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission oversees management of Florida's fish and wildlife resources, hunting and fishing regulations, and conservation efforts across the state. Commission members are appointed by the governor and require Senate confirmation.
